the toxicity of metal compounds is due to oxidative damage.

the role of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species in the toxicity of various metal ions and the mechanisms by which these species may cause tissue damage.

the role of reactive oxygen and reactive nitrogen species, including superoxide, nitric oxide, hydrogen peroxide and hydroxyl radicals, as well as lipid peroxidation and DNA damage in the toxicities produced by various metal ions.

oxidative damage is associated with most of the toxicities of the metal ions that were examined.
oxidative stress is a major mechanism in the toxicity of metals.

metal-induced oxidative stress is a significant factor in metal toxicity.

the production of reactive species is not the primary mechanism of toxicity of most metal ions; however, reactive species can be produced and may play a role in the toxicities that are associated with these ions.

the oxidative damage associated with metal ions may not be due solely to the direct effects of the metal ions themselves, but rather to the generation of reactive oxygen species that may be produced by redox cycling of the metal ions.
